item.title: Metasurface Information Processor Based on 4D Bionic Hardware and Software for Ultralow Energy Consumption Computing
item.description: As AI technology faces an energy crisis, one promising solution is bionic ultra-low energy computing hardware, which can operate at a power level as low as sub-20-watt based on the 4D model of Ca 2+ channels recently verified in brain information processing. Inspired by this model, here we design and fabricate a 4D bionic computing system based on information metasurface array with the powerful capability of electromagnetic controls. Paired with specific algorithms, each metasurface cell functions as a multifunctional unit, capable of storing, regulating, transmitting, and computing information simultaneously. The metasurface array also has high energy efficiency and precision required for high-performance bionic computing. Integrated with the DNA computing, this system is expected to achieve a variety of functions including DNA replication, DNA logical computation, and DNA produce/readout. We aim to pave the way for a new paradigm in advanced computational materials that meet the evolving demands of AI and robotics.

item.title: A Bipartite Quantum-Acoustic Architecture Stabilizes Multi-Exciton Solitons at 323 K
item.description: A fundamental thermal paradox has constrained the physical viability of quantum coherent Davydov solitons in protein α-helices for over 50 years. At 323 K (0.0278 eV), ambient thermal noise disrupts the localized amide I self-trapping resonance, rapidly scattering multi-quanta excitations into delocalized thermal states on femtosecond timescales. A non-equilibrium, bipartite quantum-acoustic stabilization matrix resolves this long-standing decoherence gap by inducing a transverse acoustic viscoelastic phonon gap, extending exciton coherence lifetimes from 6.5 fs to 42.6 fs—a pre-thermalization window sufficient to outpace non-radiative dissipation and electrostatically prime catalytic interfaces prior to microsecond motor stepping. Utilizing non-Markovian open quantum system simulations, we demonstrate that a highly polarizable variable-dipole linactant at the lipid raft interface induces localized electrodynamic Stark defects, breaking lattice translation symmetry to anchor the wave packet. Sustaining this protective boundary against passive diffusive loss mandates a strict kinetic equilibrium that arrests uncoupled proton leaks, directly coupling the continuous, hydrogen-bonded α-helices of eukaryotic F/V-type rotary c-rings to a hyper-rigid viscoelastic membrane locked in a far-from-equilibrium state. Finally, we present a definitive pathway to bypass thermal decoherence by establishing three physical boundary conditions to translate these biological principles into a predictive blueprint for synthetic quantum-acoustic metamaterials.
